checklist.note: Every behaviour the plan's Task 1 enumerates is implemented in _model_qualifiers/_model_contradicts and pinned by test_model_contradiction_matrix, in both directions: same-suffix consistent, disjoint bases contradict, different suffixes contradict, report-dropped suffix contradicts, request-omitted suffix consistent, non-trailing qualifier recognised, and the two PR#79 regression cases keep their prior answers. The fixture uses the model= kwarg on _repo as the plan directs.
Exactly the three declared files change; no caller, config, event, or state change, matching the plan's stated architecture.

Single regex constant plus a small pure helper; docstrings state the asymmetry and its rationale; both edited lines stay under the 100-char ruff limit; _model_family (the only other model comparator, used for require_distinct_model_families) is correctly left alone since qualifiers must not make two variants count as distinct families.

Three minor gaps: a reported id that reduces to an empty base after qualifier stripping now never contradicts (a behaviour change vs. the old substring test); the qualifier rule is asymmetric only in the drop direction, so a fully-qualified request with no qualifier is still satisfied by a report carrying one; and the frozenset's order/multiplicity-insensitivity — the exact shape prior finding EC-1 named — is not pinned by any test.

No user-facing doc describes the model-contradiction rule (cli-reference.md and README do not mention actual_model), so nothing external needed updating. But the new plan doc cites test line numbers that the same commit invalidated.

findings.summary: A reported model id that reduces to an empty base after qualifier stripping now satisfies any request. _model_contradicts("opus", "[1m]") returned True before this change (neither string contained the other) and returns False after: act_base is "", so `act_base not in req_base` is False and the pair is judged consistent. The pre-strip guard only exempts a wholly empty/blank identifier, so a non-empty but base-less producer report (a malformed modelUsage key, e.g. "[1m]") now bypasses the tampering guard entirely instead of being rejected.

The qualifier containment is asymmetric only against dropping, so a fully-qualified request that deliberately carries no qualifier is silently satisfied by a report that adds one. Requested "claude-opus-5", reported "claude-opus-5[1m]" is judged consistent (and is pinned that way by the "report is merely more specific" matrix row), yet by the change's own rationale — the contract froze one context-window variant and the producer answered with another — that is the same failure as the dropped-suffix case this change adds. The more-specific-report doctrine is sound for an alias resolving to a dated id, but absence of a bracketed qualifier denotes a specific default variant rather than an unresolved alias, so a repo pinning the standard variant for cost gets no protection in that direction.

Nothing pins the set semantics that motivated using a frozenset rather than a trailing-token comparison. The matrix covers a non-trailing qualifier but never a multi-qualifier pair — e.g. requested "opus[1m][beta]" against reported "claude-opus-5[beta][1m]" (order-insensitive) or a duplicate qualifier — which is exactly the shape prior finding EC-1 named. The current implementation handles them, but an inverted or list-based rewrite would pass the whole suite.

The plan cites `tests/unit/cli/test_review_runs.py:1121,1134` for the two pre-existing regression tests, but the same commit's four-line growth of the _repo signature moved them to 1125 and 1138. As committed, line 1121 lands inside _import_run's argv list and 1134 inside the first test's body, so a reader following the citation lands on unrelated code.

prior_findings.note: _model_qualifiers now collects every bracketed qualifier anywhere in the id via findall and compares frozensets, so 'claude-opus-5[1m]-20260101' and a second qualifier both parse correctly; pinned by the "qualifier need not be the trailing token" matrix row. Remaining gap is only the untested multi-qualifier case, filed separately as EC-4.
